\section*{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\paragraph{Full-replacement vs.\ accumulation.}
The primary benchmark uses full-replacement recursive chains, where each depth fully replaces the prior training corpus.
Real-world contamination typically involves accumulation, where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate}.
We evaluate accumulation at 25\% synthetic mixing on three cells (GPT-2~XL nucleus, OLMo temperature, Pythia nucleus): overall accuracy drops 13--15\,pp (70--74\%) relative to full-replacement, but $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ is preserved in all three cells (d2-vs-d3 AUC: 0.73--0.76).
Full-replacement results therefore represent an accuracy ceiling but not an EDD ceiling; depth boundaries remain discriminable under realistic mixing at 1--1.5B scale.
Extension to higher mixing ratios (50\%, 75\%) and larger models remains future work.

\paragraph{Scale and generalization boundaries.}
The primary benchmark uses 1--1.5B parameter models with controlled LoRA fine-tuning.
At 14B, cross-reference accuracy drops to 44.1\% with $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$ (nucleus/temperature); reference-model choice accounts for ${\sim}$7\,pp of the apparent degradation, and the remaining signal attenuation constitutes a scale-dependent boundary for the current feature set.
Cross-strategy transfer drops d1--d3 accuracy to 45.9\%, and on web-crawl data (C4) false positive rates reach 22\%; these gaps narrow with confidence thresholding and strategy-aware pipelines but are not fully resolved.
The pipeline depends on a fixed reference model: cross-architecture references degrade accuracy by 4--11\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:ref_ablation}), and no principled selection criterion exists beyond empirical ablation; practitioner deployments must choose a reference model without ground-truth depth labels.
Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024} achieves statistically equivalent accuracy (78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%, $p{>}0.05$) when calibrated with RF on 11 features, though it requires two forward passes (observer + performer) versus our single-model pipeline; the computational trade-off favors our approach for large-scale auditing but Binoculars may be preferred when a second model is already available.
Additional caveats (single LoRA seed, ${\sim}$1--3\,pp uncertainty; adversarial robustness; passage length sensitivity) are detailed in the Appendix.

\section*{Ethics Statement}

This work uses publicly available pretrained language models (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2~XL) and Wikipedia text as seed data.
No human subjects were involved, no private or sensitive data were collected, and no new models were released.
Our method is intended to support data provenance and training-data auditing; we acknowledge that depth estimation tools could in principle be misused to circumvent content moderation, though such risks are shared with all detection-oriented research.
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
AI assistants were used in an auxiliary role for coding support and language polishing.
All scientific decisions, experimental design, analysis, and core writing were conducted by the authors.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Model Collapse Theory.}
Recursive training on model outputs erodes distributional tails \cite{shumailov2024_nature}, an effect formalized as exponential tail decay via scaling laws \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails,seddik2024synthetic} and extended to autophagous loops in the MAD framework \cite{alemohammad2024_mad} and Markovian generation chains \cite{geng2026_markovian}.
Subsequent work refines the conditions under which collapse occurs: \citet{bertrand2024_stability} identify convergence to a fixed point under mixed real-synthetic retraining (providing theoretical grounding for our EDD ceiling, \S\ref{sec:method:theory}), \citet{shi2025_closer_look} reframe collapse as a generalization-to-memorization transition, and \citet{dohmatob2025_strong_collapse} extend guarantees to broader model classes.
Mitigation \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate,drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse,yi2026_escaping_collapse,falahati2026_curated,wenzek2020_ccnet}, data scaling under constraint \cite{muennighoff2023scaling}, non-monotonic dynamics \cite{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement}, convergence analysis \cite{marchi2024_heat_death,wang2026_contamination,knowledge_collapse2025,dohmatob2024_demystified}, and diversity decline \cite{guo2024curious,briesch2024selfconsuming,padmakumar2024diversity,sigma2026_spectral,synthetic_eggs2026} are active areas.
\citet{kazdan2025_collapse_or_thrive} systematically compare training workflows and show that data accumulation avoids collapse while pure replacement does not; \citet{suresh2025_rate_collapse} characterize the rate of collapse for fundamental distributions under recursive maximum-likelihood estimation.
\citet{schaeffer2025} argue that ``model collapse'' conflates multiple phenomena and call for operationally precise metrics; we respond by operationalizing tail-erosion predictions into a deployable ordinal classifier that reveals strategy-dependent trajectories and non-monotonic 7B behavior that the theory does not predict.
All assume depth is known a priori; we address the inverse problem of estimating depth from text alone.

\paragraph{AI Text Detection.}
The detection literature \cite{wu2025_detection_survey} spans statistical methods (DetectGPT \cite{mitchell2023_detectgpt}, Fast-DetectGPT \cite{fast_detectgpt2024}, Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, DivEye \cite{diveye2026}, BiScope \cite{guo2024_biscope}, GLTR \cite{gehrmann2019_gltr}, Ghostbuster \cite{verma2024_ghostbuster}, DNA-GPT \cite{yang2024_dnagpt}), geometric approaches based on intrinsic dimensionality \cite{tulchinskii2023_intrinsic_dim}, and watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark}, with known limits from paraphrasing \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase}, distribution shift \cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}, and generator barriers \cite{pu2026_generator_barrier}.
\citet{wang2023_seqxgpt} address sentence-level attribution by using log-probability features from white-box LLMs.
M4-SemEval \cite{wang2024_m4_semeval}, MAGE \cite{li2024_mage}, and the PAN 2026 shared tasks \cite{bevendorff2026_pan} benchmark detection across domains, models, and adversarial conditions; RAID \cite{dugan2024_raid} targets binary detection across diverse attack vectors rather than ordinal depth estimation, making direct protocol adoption inapplicable to our task.
\citet{bevendorff2025_two_paradigms} distinguish authorship attribution (which model?) from verification (human or AI?); depth estimation introduces a third axis: which recursive iteration.
All these methods perform binary classification, discarding ordinal depth information; our approach outputs ordinal depth labels, complementing rather than replacing binary detection.

\paragraph{Membership Inference and Data Provenance.}
\citet{carlini2021_extracting} demonstrate that training data can be extracted from LLMs, motivating provenance-aware pipelines.
Min-K\% Prob \cite{shi2024_minkprob} detects pretraining membership via low-probability token statistics, related to our perplexity features but limited to binary classification; Datamodels \cite{ilyas2022datamodels} trace predictions to influential training examples; cryptographically undetectable watermarks \cite{christ2024_undetectable} require generator cooperation.
TROVE \cite{zhu2025_trove} introduces fine-grained sentence-level provenance tracing with relationship classification, but targets source attribution rather than recursive depth.
Depth estimation occupies a distinct niche: ordinal, retroactive, and cooperation-free.

\paragraph{Adjacent Tasks.}
EditLens \cite{editlens2026} estimates editing extent but does not model recursive chains; \citet{uchendu2020_attribution} classify \emph{which} model generated text; \citet{mohamed2025_broken_telephone} characterize \emph{how} text degrades under iterative generation without classifying which iteration a passage comes from.
Our task performs the inverse: ordinal depth estimation from text alone.

\paragraph{Ordinal Classification.}
CORAL \cite{coral2020} enforces rank consistency via ordered binary tasks; CLOC \cite{cloc2025} extends contrastive learning with multi-margin ordinal losses; \citet{kasa2024_ordinality} benchmark ordinal techniques for NLP; \citet{janitza2016_ordinal_rf} show RF implicitly respects ordinal structure when inter-class distances are monotonic.
We adopt CORAL and CLOC as baselines (\S\ref{sec:generalization}).

\paragraph{Decoding Strategy Effects.}
Decoding strategies shape text statistics in ways that interact with depth signals \cite{holtzman2020_nucleus,finlayson2024_closing,garces_arias2025_decoding_decoded,wiher2022_decoding,basu2021_mirostat}.
Our atlas (\S\ref{sec:atlas}) shows these strategies induce qualitatively different degradation trajectories under recursive generation.

# Paper Banana — LLM 驱动的学术图表生成

PaperBanana 由 Gemini 自动写 matplotlib 代码，VLM Critic 评估渲染结果并迭代优化（默认 3 轮），输出 NeurIPS 风格 300 DPI 图表。

## 适用范围（与 paper-visualization.skill.md L4 路由一致）

| 场景 | 推荐工具 | 原因 |
|------|---------|------|
| **概念图**（架构图、流程图、framework 示意） | **PaperBanana** | matplotlib 手写 boxes/arrows/icons 极痛苦，LLM 生成代码更灵活 |
| **统计图**（scatter、bar、line、heatmap、forest） | **matplotlib 手写** | 确定性、可控、有模板 |
| **探索性图**，不确定 layout | **PaperBanana** | LLM 多轮迭代试错 |
| 离线 / 无 GOOGLE_API_KEY | **matplotlib 手写** | 不依赖外部 API |

> **核心定位**：PaperBanana 的真正优势是**概念图**——这类图没有数据输入、是纯视觉布局，手写 matplotlib 代码极其繁琐。统计图有成熟模板（见 `draw-paper-figure.skill.md`），手写更可控。
>
> **与 draw-paper-figure 的区别**：draw-paper-figure 是手写模板（快、可控、确定性）；paper-banana 是 LLM 自动生成代码（慢、灵活、适合新图类型）。

## 前置条件：GOOGLE_API_KEY

```bash
# 检查 key 是否已配置
ssh_execute("echo $GOOGLE_API_KEY | head -c 10")

# 如未配置，需要用户提供 key，然后：
ssh_execute("echo 'export GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED]' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc")

# 安装 PaperBanana
ssh_execute("pip install paperbanana -q")

# 验证安装
ssh_execute("paperbanana --version")
```

**⚠️ 如果 GOOGLE_API_KEY 未设置，直接停下来问用户要 key，不要尝试绕过。**

**⚠️ 中国大陆服务器访问 Gemini API 可能被墙。** 先测试连通性：`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`，超时则需设置代理或改用海外服务器。

## 用法一：概念图（主要用途）

概念图没有数据文件输入，靠 `--intent` 描述布局、组件、箭头、颜色语义。

```bash
# Framework / Pipeline 图
ssh_execute("""
cd ~/my-project && \
GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED] paperbanana plot \
  --intent "Three-stage pipeline diagram flowing left to right:
Stage 1 'Data Collection' (blue rounded box) with icons for web scraping and API,
Stage 2 'Processing' (green rounded box) with sub-steps filter/transform/validate stacked vertically,
Stage 3 'Model Training' (orange rounded box) with GPU icon.
Connect stages with thick arrows. Add a feedback loop arrow from Stage 3 back to Stage 1 (dashed, gray).
Below the pipeline, a horizontal bar showing 'Time: 2h → 6h → 24h'.
White background, no border, publication quality 300 DPI." \
  --iterations 3
""")

# 架构图（多组件 + 交互）
ssh_execute("""
cd ~/my-project && \
GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED] paperbanana plot \
  --intent "System architecture diagram:
Top layer: 'User Interface' (light blue rectangle, full width).
Middle layer: three equal boxes side by side — 'Auth Service', 'API Gateway', 'Cache' (all light green).
Bottom layer: two boxes — 'Database' (left, wider) and 'Message Queue' (right, narrower).
Vertical arrows connecting layers. Horizontal dashed arrow between Database and Message Queue.
Each box has a small icon in top-left corner. Rounded corners, drop shadow, white background." \
  --iterations 3
""")
```

### 概念图意图描述技巧

- **明确空间布局**：left-to-right / top-to-bottom / grid，不要让 LLM 猜
- **指定组件形状**：rounded box / circle / diamond / hexagon
- **颜色绑定语义**：和论文其他图一致（如 baseline=blue, treatment=orange）
- **箭头类型**：solid / dashed / thick / thin / bidirectional
- **标注所有文字**：每个 box 的 label、箭头上的 annotation

## 用法二：探索性统计图

已有模板的统计图（heatmap、scatter、bar）优先用 `draw-paper-figure`。PaperBanana 适合新图类型或不确定 layout 的探索。

```bash
# CSV 数据 + 意图描述
ssh_execute("""
cd ~/my-project && \
GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED] paperbanana plot \
  --data results/delta_ece_summary.csv \
  --intent "Diverging heatmap showing ΔECE (quantized minus FP16) for 4 PTQ methods across 6 datasets and 5 models, red=calibration degraded blue=improved, annotate significant cells with asterisk" \
  --iterations 3
""")

# JSON 数据
ssh_execute("""
cd ~/my-project && \
GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED] paperbanana plot \
  --data results/tstar_by_dataset.json \
  --intent "Line plot showing T* values across 6 datasets for 5 LLM models, highlight three regime zones with background shading"
""")
```

## 数据格式准备（统计图）

PaperBanana 接受 CSV（列名清晰）或 JSON（字典格式）：

```python
prep_script = """
import csv
data = [
    {'model': 'LLaMA-3.1-8B', 'method': 'GPTQ', 'dataset': 'ARC-C', 'delta_ece': -18.7, 'sig': True},
    {'model': 'LLaMA-3.1-8B', 'method': 'AWQ',  'dataset': 'TruthfulQA', 'delta_ece': +17.6, 'sig': False},
    # ... 完整数据
]
with open('results/summary.csv', 'w', newline='') as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['model','method','dataset','delta_ece','sig'])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(data)
print("CSV ready")
"""
ssh_execute(f"cd ~/my-project && python3 -c '{prep_script}'")
```

## 输出处理

```bash
# 找最新生成的图
ssh_execute("""
latest=$(ls -td ~/my-project/outputs/run_*/ | head -1)
echo "Latest: $latest"
ls "$latest"
""")

# 复制到 figures/paper/ 并转 PDF
ssh_execute("""
latest=$(ls -td ~/my-project/outputs/run_*/ | head -1)
cp "$latest"/*.png ~/my-project/figures/paper/
cd ~/my-project/figures/paper/
for f in *.png; do
    python3 -c "
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.image as mpimg
img = mpimg.imread('$f')
h, w = img.shape[:2]
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(w/300, h/300), dpi=300)
ax = fig.add_axes([0,0,1,1])
ax.imshow(img); ax.axis('off')
plt.savefig('${f%.png}.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', pad_inches=0)
plt.close()
print('PDF:', '${f%.png}.pdf')
"
done
""")
```

## 迭代优化

```bash
# 查看 Critic 的评估反馈
ssh_execute("""
latest=$(ls -td ~/my-project/outputs/run_*/ | head -1)
cat "$latest/metadata.json" | python3 -m json.tool | grep -A5 "critic"
""")

# 重跑时加强意图描述（加更多约束）
ssh_execute("""
GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED] paperbanana plot \
  --intent "... [更具体的空间布局 / 颜色语义 / 组件关系描述] ..." \
  --iterations 5
""")
```

## 注意事项

- 每张图大约消耗 3-5 次 Gemini API 调用（3 轮迭代），Gemini free tier 够用
- 生成时间 1-3 分钟/图（含 LLM 调用 + 本地执行）
- 如果服务器无法访问 Gemini，改用 `draw-paper-figure`（完全离线）
- 概念图的 intent 描述越详细越好——空间布局、组件关系、颜色语义都要写清楚

In this work, we focus on the 1--1.5B parameter regime under \emph{controlled full-replacement chains}, where each generation fully replaces the prior training set, isolating the depth variable. Real-world contamination typically involves partial mixing (accumulation), where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions; the full-replacement setting provides an upper bound on depth signal strength, and we discuss implications for accumulation settings in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.
